Sangheon Pack Wins KICS Haedong Academic Award
Professor Sangheon Pack of the School of Electrical Engineering at Korea University’s College of Engineering has been named the recipient of the 2026 Haedong Academic Award by the Korean Institute of Communications and Information Sciences (KICS). He was recognized for his research in software-based networking and intelligent networks for 5G and 6G. ee.korea.ac.kr
The Haedong Awards were established in 1990 to recognize outstanding researchers and encourage research in electrical engineering and related fields. The awards are supported by the Haedong Science and Culture Foundation, founded by the late Jeong-sik Kim, former chairman of Daeduck Electronics. KICS has selected recipients for the awards since 2005. The Haedong Academic Award recognizes significant contributions to the field over the preceding 10 years, including research published in KICS journals and SCI-indexed international journals. ee.korea.ac.kr
Since joining Korea University in 2007, Professor Pack has published approximately 170 papers in SCI-indexed journals. His previous honors include the IEEE Communications Society Asia Pacific Board Outstanding Young Researcher Award, the KICS Haedong Young Scholar Award, the IEEE/IEIE IT Young Engineer Award, and the KIISE Young Information Scientist Award. ee.korea.ac.kr
The award ceremony is scheduled for 5 p.m. on Friday, December 4, 2026, at Hotel Samjung in Seoul.

College of Engineering Welcomes Harbin Institute of Technology Delegation
On November 13, the Korea University College of Engineering welcomed a delegation from Harbin Institute of Technology (HIT) in China for a meeting on academic exchange and a tour of key teaching and research facilities.
The visit followed a July visit by HIT students and university officials. This time, the delegation included senior university officials, faculty members, and staff responsible for international cooperation. In its invitation, the College of Engineering proposed several topics for discussion, including recommendations for prospective graduate students, opportunities for joint doctoral supervision and training, and the exchange of recent research findings.
Dean Gil Soo Jang, Associate Dean for Academic Affairs Ji-Hun Seo, and other representatives of the College of Engineering attended the meeting in Room 114 of the Engineering Building. Associate Dean Seo gave an overview of the College’s teaching and research activities. Representatives from both universities then discussed opportunities for future academic exchange and collaboration in areas of mutual interest.
After the meeting, the delegation toured College of Engineering facilities in the Innovation Building and the New Engineering Building. In the Innovation Building, Professor Seok Chung of the School of Mechanical Engineering introduced key teaching and research facilities. In the New Engineering Building, Professor Sang Bin Lee of the School of Electrical Engineering and Professor Wangyun Won of the Department of Chemical and Biological Engineering showed the visitors around their respective facilities.
Founded in 1920, Harbin Institute of Technology is a leading Chinese research university and a member of the C9 League, an alliance of nine major research universities in China. HIT is known for its strengths in engineering and is active in teaching and research across a range of disciplines.

Jae Won Shim’s Team Publishes Indoor Solar Cell Review in Nature
A research team led by Professor Jae Won Shim of the School of Electrical Engineering at Korea University has published a review article in Nature, presenting commercialization strategies for next-generation indoor photovoltaics that generate electricity from indoor lighting. The article was published online on November 5, with Dr. Tae Hyuk Kim as the first author and Professor Shim as the sole corresponding author.
Indoor photovoltaics convert light from sources such as LEDs and fluorescent lamps into electricity. The technology is attracting attention as a potential solution for reducing the need for battery replacement in Internet of Things (IoT) devices and smart-home sensors. However, indoor lighting is much weaker than sunlight, and its spectral distribution varies depending on the light source, requiring materials and device designs tailored to indoor environments.
The team comprehensively analyzed major indoor photovoltaic technologies, including perovskite, organic, amorphous silicon, III–V compound semiconductor, and dye-sensitized solar cells. Based on this analysis, the review presented development strategies across the commercialization process, from material selection and device design to large-area module fabrication, performance evaluation, and integration with electronic devices.
The researchers emphasized the need to consider manufacturing costs, long-term stability, and environmental and safety issues alongside high power-conversion efficiency. They also highlighted the importance of integrated system design, combining photovoltaic devices with power-management integrated circuits and energy-storage components to store and deliver electricity efficiently. These approaches are expected to help reduce battery replacement and maintenance requirements for low-power electronic devices in smart homes and smart buildings.
“This review comprehensively analyzes the strengths and limitations of various indoor photovoltaic technologies and identifies concrete directions for translating laboratory research into commercially viable products,” said Professor Shim.

60 Years of Growth with the Dream of the Nation:
College of Engineering, Korea University
Korea University College of Technology, which trains creative engineering leaders, has signed MOUs with more than 600 universities and domestic and foreign companies around the world to foster international and professional engineering talents. At the age of 20, Korea University's College of Engineering will join us in the great emergency toward an endless dream.
Korea University College of Engineering has developed along with the growth history of Korea and Korea, which are in the ranks of advanced countries with cutting-edge technology based on basic science.
The College of Engineering, which has grown under the reputation of Korea University, is now taking a new leap forward to lead the development of Korea University with 300,000 friends.
